name: The Kings of the Kingdom of Judah
dom: the southern Davidic monarchy; kings of Judah from Rehoboam to Zedekiah
note: The succession of Davidic kings who ruled the southern Kingdom of Judah from the division of the monarchy until the Babylonian destruction of Jerusalem.

name: The Kings of the Northern Kingdom of Israel
dom: the breakaway northern monarchy; the dynasties of Israel
note: The succession of kings, across several dynasties, who ruled the breakaway northern Kingdom of Israel until its fall to Assyria.

name: Rehoboam
dom: the division of the monarchy; first king of Judah; harsh counsel
note: Son of Solomon whose refusal to lighten the people's burden provoked the northern tribes to secede, leaving him king of Judah alone.

name: Asa
dom: cultic reform; removal of idols; war with Baasha
note: King of Judah praised for removing idols and reforming worship, who relied on an alliance with Aram against the northern kingdom.

name: Jehoshaphat
dom: judicial reform; teaching of the law; alliance with Ahab
note: King of Judah remembered for instituting judges and Levitical teaching and for his ill-fated alliance with Ahab of Israel.

name: Ahaz
dom: apostasy; the Syro-Ephraimite crisis; Assyrian vassalage
note: King of Judah condemned for idolatry who sought Assyrian protection against Aram and Israel during the Syro-Ephraimite war.

name: Uzziah (Azariah)
dom: military expansion; building; the leprous king
note: Long-reigning king of Judah who expanded the kingdom but was struck with leprosy after presuming to offer incense in the Temple.

name: Hezekiah
dom: cultic reform; deliverance from Sennacherib; the Siloam tunnel
note: Reforming king of Judah who centralized worship, withstood the Assyrian siege of Jerusalem, and was granted fifteen added years of life.

name: Manasseh (king of Judah)
dom: idolatry and bloodshed; the longest reign; later repentance
note: Longest-reigning king of Judah, condemned for grievous idolatry, whom Chronicles portrays as repenting after Assyrian captivity.

name: Josiah
dom: the great reform; the rediscovered book of the law; covenant renewal
note: Reforming king of Judah who, on the discovery of the book of the law, purged idolatry and renewed the covenant before dying at Megiddo.

name: Zedekiah
dom: the last king of Judah; rebellion against Babylon; the fall of Jerusalem
note: Last king of Judah, installed by Nebuchadnezzar, whose rebellion brought the Babylonian destruction of Jerusalem and his own blinding and exile.

name: Jeroboam I
dom: the northern secession; the golden calves of Dan and Bethel
note: First king of the breakaway northern Kingdom of Israel, who set up golden calves at Dan and Bethel and became the archetype of sinful kingship.

name: Omri
dom: dynastic founder; the building of Samaria
note: Northern king who founded a powerful dynasty and built Samaria as the capital of the Kingdom of Israel.

name: Ahab
dom: the Baal cult; conflict with Elijah; the house of Omri
note: Son of Omri and king of Israel who, married to Jezebel, promoted the worship of Baal and was repeatedly opposed by the prophet Elijah.

name: Jehu
dom: the purge of the house of Omri; zeal against Baal
note: Northern king anointed at Elisha's direction who overthrew the house of Omri, killed Jezebel, and exterminated the worship of Baal in Israel.

name: Jeroboam II
dom: territorial restoration; prosperity; the era of Amos and Hosea
note: Long-reigning northern king under whom Israel reached its greatest extent, the setting for the prophets Amos and Hosea.

name: Jezebel
dom: promotion of Baal worship; persecution of the prophets; the Naboth affair
note: Phoenician wife of Ahab who promoted Baal worship, persecuted Yahweh's prophets, and engineered the death of Naboth before her own violent end.

name: Goliath
dom: the Philistine champion; the duel at the Valley of Elah
note: Philistine giant of Gath whose challenge to Israel was answered and ended by the young David with a sling and stone.

name: Jonathan (son of Saul)
dom: valor against the Philistines; covenant friendship with David
note: Eldest son of Saul, a brave warrior bound to David in covenant friendship, who fell with his father at the battle of Mount Gilboa.

name: Absalom
dom: rebellion against David; the usurpation; death in the oak
note: Handsome son of David who rose in rebellion to seize the throne and was killed by Joab after his hair caught in an oak.

name: Boaz
dom: the kinsman-redeemer; the marriage to Ruth; ancestor of David
note: Wealthy Bethlehemite who acted as kinsman-redeemer, married Ruth, and became the great-grandfather of King David.

name: Naomi
dom: bereavement and return; the bond with Ruth; restoration
note: Bethlehemite widow who returned from Moab with her daughter-in-law Ruth and was restored through the birth of Obed, ancestor of David.

name: Naaman
dom: foreign general; leprosy and healing; the seven dippings in the Jordan
note: Commander of the army of Aram, cured of leprosy by washing seven times in the Jordan at the word of the prophet Elisha.

name: Balaam
dom: divination; the speaking donkey; blessing instead of cursing Israel
note: Mesopotamian seer hired by Balak of Moab to curse Israel who, restrained by Yahweh and his speaking donkey, blessed them instead.

name: Delilah
dom: seduction and betrayal; the secret of Samson's strength
note: Woman of the Valley of Sorek who, bribed by the Philistine lords, coaxed from Samson the secret of his strength and betrayed him.

name: Nebuchadnezzar II
dom: the conqueror of Jerusalem; the Babylonian exile; the dream visions
note: King of Babylon who destroyed Jerusalem and its Temple and carried Judah into exile, and whose dreams and madness frame the early chapters of Daniel.

name: Cyrus the Great
dom: the conqueror of Babylon; the edict of return; the Lord's anointed shepherd
note: Persian king who conquered Babylon and issued the decree permitting the exiles to return and rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem.

name: The Seven Deacons (Acts 6)
dom: the seven chosen to serve tables and oversee the daily distribution
note: The Seven chosen in Acts 6 to oversee the daily distribution to widows, traditionally regarded as the first deacons; named members include Stephen the protomartyr and Philip the Evangelist.

name: The Myrrh-Bearing Women
dom: the women who came to anoint Jesus' body; first witnesses of the Resurrection
note: The Myrrh-Bearing Women (Myrophoroi) who brought spices to anoint Jesus' body and became the first witnesses of the Resurrection; commemorated as a group in Eastern tradition.

name: James the Just
dom: first bishop of Jerusalem; leader of the Jerusalem council; the Epistle of James
note: James 'the Lord's brother' (Gal 1:19), distinct from the apostolic Jameses, who presided over the Jerusalem church and the council of Acts 15 and is the traditional author of the Epistle of James.

name: Jude (Brother of the Lord)
dom: traditional author of the Epistle of Jude; named among the brothers of Jesus
note: Jude (Judas), named among the brothers of the Lord and identified in his epistle as 'brother of James'; traditional author of the canonical Epistle of Jude, distinguished here from the apostle Jude Thaddaeus.

name: Philip the Evangelist
dom: one of the Seven Deacons; baptizer of the Ethiopian eunuch and of Samaria
note: One of the Seven chosen in Acts 6:5, later evangelizing Samaria and baptizing the Ethiopian eunuch; Acts 21:8 calls him 'the evangelist, one of the seven,' distinguishing him from the apostle Philip.

name: Silas
dom: prophet of the Jerusalem church; companion of Paul; co-sender of the Thessalonian letters
note: Silas (Silvanus), a leading man and prophet of the Jerusalem church, chosen by Paul for the second journey and imprisoned with him at Philippi; co-sender of 1-2 Thessalonians.

name: Apollos
dom: Alexandrian Jewish teacher; eloquent preacher 'mighty in the Scriptures'
note: An eloquent Alexandrian Jew 'mighty in the Scriptures,' instructed more fully by Priscilla and Aquila, then a powerful coworker at Corinth whom Paul names as a fellow planter.

name: Priscilla
dom: tentmaker and missionary; with Aquila instructed Apollos and hosted a house church
note: Priscilla (Prisca), wife of Aquila and his constant ministry partner; together they instructed Apollos and hosted a house church, she frequently named first.

name: Aquila
dom: Jewish tentmaker of Pontus; missionary coworker; host of a house church
note: Aquila, a Jew of Pontus and tentmaker, with his wife Priscilla a close coworker of Paul who instructed Apollos and hosted house churches at Ephesus and Rome.

name: Lydia of Thyatira
dom: dealer in purple cloth; first recorded European convert; host of the Philippian church
note: A God-fearing dealer in purple goods from Thyatira at Philippi whose heart 'the Lord opened'; the first named convert in Europe, whose home became the base of the Philippian church.

name: Joseph of Arimathea
dom: member of the Sanhedrin; secret disciple who provided the tomb and buried Jesus
note: A rich and respected councillor and secret disciple who asked Pilate for the body of Jesus and laid it in his own new rock-cut tomb; present in all four Gospels.

name: Mary of Bethany
dom: sister of Lazarus and Martha; sat at Jesus' feet; anointed him at Bethany
note: Sister of Martha and Lazarus, who sat at Jesus' feet to learn (Luke 10) and anointed his feet with costly nard before the Passion (John 12); distinct from Mary Magdalene.

name: Salome (the Myrrh-Bearer)
dom: Galilean woman follower; witness at the crucifixion; myrrh-bearer at the tomb
note: One of the Galilean women who followed Jesus, present at the crucifixion and among those who came to the tomb with spices; often identified with the mother of the sons of Zebedee, and distinct from Salome daughter of Herodias.

name: Zacchaeus
dom: chief tax collector at Jericho; convert who restored fourfold
note: A wealthy chief tax collector at Jericho who climbed a sycamore to see Jesus, received him, and pledged half his goods to the poor and fourfold restitution.

name: Mary, mother of James
dom: Galilean woman follower; witness at the crucifixion and empty tomb; myrrh-bearer
note: Mary the mother of James the younger and Joses, one of the Galilean women at the cross and among the myrrh-bearers who found the empty tomb ('the other Mary').

name: Pontius Pilate
dom: Roman prefect of Judaea; the judge who condemned Jesus to crucifixion
note: The Roman prefect of Judaea who tried Jesus and ordered the crucifixion; named in the creeds and confirmed epigraphically by the Pilate Stone.

name: Herod the Great
dom: Roman client king of Judaea; ordered the Massacre of the Innocents
note: Rome's client king of Judaea, the Herod of the Nativity who, alarmed by the Magi, ordered the killing of the infants of Bethlehem; abundantly attested by Josephus.

name: Herod Antipas
dom: tetrarch of Galilee and Perea; executed John the Baptist; examined Jesus
note: Tetrarch of Galilee and Perea, son of Herod the Great, who imprisoned and beheaded John the Baptist and to whom Pilate sent Jesus during the trial.

name: Caiaphas
dom: Jewish high priest; presided over the Sanhedrin trial of Jesus
note: Joseph Caiaphas, high priest who convened the Sanhedrin against Jesus and counseled that one man should die for the people; son-in-law of Annas, plausibly attested by the inscribed ossuary found in Jerusalem.

name: The Rashidun — the Rightly-Guided Caliphs
dom: the first four caliphs; rightly-guided succession; the early Islamic state
note: The first four caliphs of Islam — Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali — regarded in Sunni tradition as the 'Rightly-Guided' successors of the Prophet (632-661 CE).

name: The Sahaba — Companions of the Prophet
dom: companions of the Prophet; the first generation of Muslims; transmitters of the faith
note: The companions who knew, accompanied, or saw the Prophet Muhammad and embraced Islam, forming the first generation of Muslims and the chain of transmission for the faith.

name: Ummahat al-Mu'minin — the Mothers of the Believers
dom: wives of the Prophet; mothers of the believers
note: The wives of the Prophet Muhammad, given this honorific title in the Qur'an (33:6).

name: The Ten Promised Paradise (al-Ashara al-Mubashshara)
dom: ten companions promised paradise; elite companions
note: The ten companions whom the Prophet reportedly named as assured of paradise during their lifetimes, including Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali.

name: Abu Bakr
dom: first Rashidun caliph; closest companion of the Prophet; first adult male convert
note: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, the Prophet's closest companion and father-in-law, who became the first Rightly-Guided Caliph (632-634 CE).

name: Umar ibn al-Khattab
dom: second Rashidun caliph; expansion of the state; justice and administration
note: Umar ibn al-Khattab al-Faruq, the second Rightly-Guided Caliph (634-644 CE), under whom the early conquests greatly expanded, renowned for his austere justice.

name: Uthman ibn Affan
dom: third Rashidun caliph; the standardized Quran; early convert
note: Uthman ibn Affan, the third Rightly-Guided Caliph (644-656 CE), credited with commissioning the standardized written compilation of the Quran, and a son-in-law of the Prophet.

name: Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib
dom: uncle of the Prophet; warrior; martyr of Uhud
note: A paternal uncle of the Prophet, the celebrated warrior titled 'Lion of God,' killed at the Battle of Uhud (625 CE).

name: Bilal ibn Rabah
dom: first muezzin; early convert; formerly enslaved
note: An Abyssinian formerly enslaved and freed by Abu Bakr, an early convert and the first muezzin (caller to prayer) of Islam.

name: Salman al-Farsi
dom: Persian convert; strategist of the Trench; seeker of true religion
note: Salman the Persian, a companion who advised digging the defensive trench at the Battle of the Trench (627 CE) and was honored as a member of the Prophet's household.

name: Khalid ibn al-Walid
dom: general; military conquests; undefeated commander
note: Titled 'Sword of God,' the foremost military commander of early Islam, leading campaigns in the Ridda wars and the conquests of Iraq and Syria.

name: Abu Hurayra
dom: foremost hadith narrator; transmission of prophetic tradition
note: A companion who became the most prolific narrator of hadith in the Sunni tradition.

name: Zayd ibn Haritha
dom: adopted son of the Prophet; commander; martyr of Mu'ta
note: A freedman and adopted son of the Prophet, the only companion named in the Quran, who died as a commander at the Battle of Mu'ta (629 CE).

name: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib
dom: cousin of the Prophet; leader of the Abyssinia migration; martyr of Mu'ta
note: Brother of Ali and cousin of the Prophet, who led the migration to Abyssinia and died as a commander at Mu'ta (629 CE), titled 'Ja'far the Flyer.'

name: Abu Talib
dom: uncle and protector of the Prophet; chief of Banu Hashim; father of Ali
note: The paternal uncle who raised the orphaned Muhammad and protected him during the early Meccan persecution as chief of the Banu Hashim.

name: Abd al-Muttalib
dom: grandfather of the Prophet; chief of Quraysh; custodian of the Kaaba
note: The grandfather of the Prophet Muhammad and a leading chief of the Quraysh who served as custodian of the Kaaba in Mecca.

name: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid
dom: first wife of the Prophet; first believer; merchant patron
note: The first wife of the Prophet Muhammad, a wealthy Meccan merchant and the first person to accept Islam.

name: Aisha bint Abi Bakr
dom: wife of the Prophet; hadith narrator and scholar; daughter of Abu Bakr
note: A wife of the Prophet and daughter of Abu Bakr, who became a foremost narrator of hadith and authority on Islamic law and tradition.
